walkthroughs.body_html:
Data Types & Structures — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Data Types & Structures brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Data Types & Structures.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which item is removed first from a stack?
options: The most recently added (top) - LIFO.
Encrypting data so it cannot be read.
Any item, randomly.
The first one added (FIFO).

mcqs.q: What does in-order traversal of a binary search tree produce?
options: Nodes in ascending sorted order.
Any item, randomly.
Only the root node.
Nodes in the order they were inserted.
Putting code inside other code (nesting).
Only the root node.
Encrypting data so it cannot be read.
Bundling data and methods together while restricting direct access to internal state.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Stack overflow”?
options: Fixed-size array queue where rear wraps to front, avoiding wasted space.
Double-ended queue allowing insertion and removal from both front and back.
Error when more items are pushed than the stack can hold (or recursion is too deep).
FIFO abstract data type with enqueue and dequeue; used for scheduling and BFS.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Priority queue”?
options: FIFO abstract data type with enqueue and dequeue; used for scheduling and BFS.
LIFO abstract data type supporting push, pop and peek; used in function calls and undo.
Error when more items are pushed than the stack can hold (or recursion is too deep).
Queue where elements are dequeued in order of priority rather than insertion order.
